name: R1-Searcher: Incentivizing the Search Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2503.05592); submitted 7 Mar 2025, last revised 18 Mar 2025. Not yet a peer-reviewed venue at time of survey.
authors_affiliation: Huatong Song, Jinhao Jiang, Yingqian Min, Jie Chen, Zhipeng Chen, Wayne Xin Zhao, Lei Fang, Ji-Rong Wen. Primary affiliation: Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China; with DataCanvas Alaya NeW (Lei Fang). Correspondence: Wayne Xin Zhao.
task_domain: QA (open-domain / knowledge-intensive multi-hop question answering with autonomous tool/search invocation during reasoning).
problem_setting: Train a single LLM to autonomously decide when to invoke an external search system and how to integrate retrieved documents into its chain-of-thought to answer multi-hop questions. Setting is interactive (the model emits queries and the retrieval environment returns documents mid-generation), single-agent, and supervision is outcome-only (final-answer correctness via F1 plus format/retrieval rewards); no process rewards, no SFT cold start, and no intermediate-step annotations are used. Works from both an Instruct model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and a Base model (Qwen-2.5-7B-Base) trained purely with RL.
what_is_retrieved: Documents: 100-word Wikipedia passages (with titles) from a static corpus retrieved during reasoning; in the online-search generalization test, summarized web pages from Google Web Search.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (2019 English Wikipedia from KILT, ~29M passages); generalizes at test time to online Google Web Search. Not a growing/episodic agent memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking per query (top documents returned by the dense retriever and injected verbatim); the model issues multiple queries iteratively to cover all hops, but each individual retrieval call is fixed top-k. No explicit minimal-set/completeness objective is optimized.
retrieval_unit: document (100-word Wikipedia passage chunk with title); retrieved set injected between <begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents> tags.
index_source: Static offline corpus: English Wikipedia (KILT 2019 dump) segmented into 100-word passages, ~29M passages; index is fixed and not grown online.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index over passage embeddings (BGE-large-en-v1.5 embeddings); standard ANN/flat similarity index, no graph or hierarchy.
retriever_type: Dense retriever (BGE-large-en-v1.5 text embeddings); the LLM itself acts as a learned query generator but the document scorer is an off-the-shelf dense retriever. Online variant uses Google Web Search API + GPT-4o-mini summarization.
retriever_learning_signal: none for the retriever itself (BGE-large-en-v1.5 is frozen / off-the-shelf). The LLM's query-generation and retrieve-or-not policy is trained by outcome-based RL (Reinforce++ with modifications): Stage-1 retrieval reward (binary on whether any retrieval is invoked) + format reward; Stage-2 F1 answer reward + format reward. So the learned signal is on the policy that drives retrieval, not on the embedding model.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned keyword query generated by the LLM during its <think> reasoning; the model emits a search query (keywords only, constrained to a single triple/fact) enclosed in <begin_of_query>...<end_of_query>. Queries are produced autonomously as reasoning proceeds.
query_granularity: step/state-level: queries are generated at intermediate reasoning steps whenever the model is uncertain, allowing multiple sequential queries within one rollout (up to a maximum retrieval count of 8).
when_to_retrieve: adaptive / agent-initiated and iterative: the model itself decides at each reasoning step whether to emit a query, and can retrieve multiple times within a single solution (max 8 retrievals). Learned via RL rather than a fixed schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: retrieval fires when the LLM generates the <end_of_query> tag during reasoning (the generation pauses, the query is extracted, documents are fetched and inserted). The decision to emit a query is a learned RL policy behavior triggered by the model's own uncertainty, not an explicit confidence/attention threshold.
reranking: None. Top documents from the dense retriever are used directly; no separate reranking stage is reported.
retrieved_context_refinement: none for local Wikipedia retrieval (documents injected verbatim within tags). For the online-search generalization setting only, retrieved web pages are summarized/compressed by GPT-4o-mini before integration due to page length.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation as a training signal loop: retrieved documents are inserted into the model's ongoing reasoning context (<begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents>) and the model continues reasoning conditioned on them; the entire retrieve-and-reason trajectory is optimized end-to-end by outcome RL (reward maximization).
planning_integration: per-step interleaved inside a single autoregressive reasoning loop: retrieve-then-reason cycles repeat within one rollout (RAG-based rollout). The model plans, queries, reads documents, and continues reasoning iteratively until producing the final <answer>. Not MCTS/tree search (explicitly contrasted with MCTS test-time scaling baselines).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-reasoning-step / per-tool-call within a rollout: retrieval is woven into the chain-of-thought at the point each search query is emitted, so multiple retrieve-read-reason cycles occur per solution.
retrieved_item_representation: raw retrieved passages (verbatim Wikipedia text inside <begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents> tags) injected into the reasoning context; in the online setting, GPT-4o-mini summaries of web pages.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: raw document passage (factual evidence text); not distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retrieval Mask-based Loss Calculation: <begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents> tokens are treated as special tokens and masked out of the RL loss so retrieved (environment) tokens do not influence policy gradients; combined with strict format rewards (iteratively refined to prevent reward hacking such as fabricating documents without querying). Robustness to noisy/irrelevant retrieval emerges from end-to-end outcome RL exploration rather than an explicit relevance evaluator.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory). Retrieval targets a fixed external corpus; learned 'memory' is implicit in the model's RL-updated weights, not an external retrievable store.
write_back: false. The system does not write new experiences/cases/skills into any external memory store at inference time; learning is baked into model weights via RL training only.
online_growth: false. The retrievable store (Wikipedia index) is fixed; it does not grow during deployment. Only the online-search variant queries the live web, but no agent memory is accumulated.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back mechanism; the retrievable store is static and no episodic memory is maintained).
failure_experience_usage: No explicit storage/retrieval of failed experiences as memory. During RL training, incorrect rollouts receive low/negative reward (e.g., F1=0, or -2 format penalty for malformed output) and thus shape the policy via gradient updates (success+failure used as contrastive RL signal), but failures are not stored as retrievable cases.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no external memory store to mutate). The policy is updated by RL gradient steps over a single training epoch; no append/dedup/refine of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: true (partial): the decision of WHEN to retrieve and WHAT query to issue is a learned RL policy (Reinforce++ with RAG rollout and retrieval-masked loss). The document scoring/ranking itself remains a fixed off-the-shelf dense retriever (BGE), not RL-optimized.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / single-agent. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing; one model trained and evaluated independently.
benchmarks: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA (2Wiki), Musique, Bamboogle. Training data selected from HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA training sets (~8148 samples total). HotpotQA and 2Wiki are in-domain; Musique and Bamboogle are out-of-domain. Bamboogle also used for online-search generalization (Google API).
baselines: Naive Generation; Standard RAG; Branching: SuRe, REPLUG; Summarization: LongLLMLingua, RECOMP, Selective-Context; Adaptive Retrieval: SKR; RAG-CoT: Self-Ask, Iter-RetGen, IRCoT; Test-Time Scaling (MCTS): CR-Planner, ReARTeR; Reasoning models with standard RAG: Marco-o1-Qwen-7B, Skywork-o1-Llama-3.1-8B. Backbones for baselines: GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Online-search comparison: Search-o1 (32B backbone).
key_metrics: Cover Exact Match (ACC_R / CEM) and LLM-as-Judge (ACC_L, using GPT-4o-mini); ablations also report EM and F1. Online-search section reports CEM.
headline_result: On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct backbone, R1-Searcher outperforms the strongest baseline ReARTeR by 48.2% on HotpotQA, 21.7% on 2WikiMultiHopQA, and 4.0% on Bamboogle (relative improvement, LLM-as-Judge ACC_L). Qwen-2.5-7B-Base trained RL-from-scratch (no cold start) reaches the best overall results (e.g., HotpotQA ACC_R 0.654 / ACC_L 0.750; 2Wiki 0.636 / 0.650; Bamboogle 0.528 / 0.544; Musique 0.282 / 0.314), surpassing closed-source GPT-4o-mini baselines.
ablations: (1) GRPO vs Reinforce++ as the RL algorithm: GRPO gives longer responses, more retrievals, and better OOD (Bamboogle) generalization; Reinforce++ is better on in-domain (HotpotQA/2Wiki) (Table 3, avg CEM 59.0 vs 58.9). (2) RL vs SFT: RL substantially beats SFT on both in-domain and OOD (e.g., Qwen-Base-RL avg CEM 60.6 vs SFT 50.1; Llama-Instruct-RL 58.2 vs SFT 48.2); SFT relies on internal knowledge and retrieves at worse timing/relevance. (3) Answer reward type (EM vs CEM vs F1): F1 is best (avg CEM 60.6) with up to +52.6% over EM (39.7); EM too strict for open-ended answers. (4) Format reward strictness needed to prevent reward hacking (e.g., fabricating documents without querying; Stage-1 needed for Llama to retrieve at all). (5) Training-data difficulty: including hard (>20 rollout) questions ('w. Difficult') improves avg CEM by ~3.4% over 'w/o Difficult' (60.8 vs 58.8). (6) Data diversity: HotpotQA+2Wiki mixture beats either alone by up to +10.9% avg CEM (60.6 mixture vs 54.6 HotpotQA / 43.6 2Wiki).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (CEM/ACC_R, LLM-as-Judge/ACC_L, EM, F1) are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics such as Recall@k or nDCG are reported (the retriever is fixed off-the-shelf).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer correctness). Process-level signals are reported qualitatively/analytically (response length, number of retrievals during training logs, case studies on retrieval timing/relevance) but not as scored process-quality metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: R1-Searcher is positioned as more efficient than MCTS-based test-time scaling (ReARTeR/CR-Planner) which 'incurs significant overhead due to increased retrieval invocations.' Max retrieval count capped at 8 per solution; 16 rollouts per sample during training, train batch 256, rollout batch 64, 1 epoch, lr 2e-6, DeepSpeed Zero-2. Number of retrievals tracked in training logs (harder data / GRPO -> more retrievals). No explicit latency/token-cost numbers vs accuracy reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k per retrieval call (top documents from dense retriever, each a 100-word passage); model may issue up to 8 retrieval calls per solution (maximum retrieval count = 8). No adaptive/precision-driven k or reranked-then-truncated budgeting reported.
builds_on: Reinforce++ (base RL algorithm, modified with RAG-based rollout + retrieval mask-based loss); DeepSeek-R1 / R1-Zero-style outcome-based RL for reasoning (incentivizing capability via RL without SFT); GRPO (compared as alternative). Backbones: Qwen-2.5-7B-Base and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Evaluation infra: FlashRAG; corpus from KILT Wikipedia; retriever BGE-large-en-v1.5; ReARTeR evaluation framework conventions.
contrasts_with: MCTS / test-time scaling RAG methods (ReARTeR, CR-Planner) which it outperforms while avoiding heavy retrieval overhead; SFT/distillation cold-start approaches (it uses RL only, no cold start); RAG-CoT prompting methods (Self-Ask, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen); branching (SuRe, REPLUG) and summarization (LongLLMLingua, RECOMP, Selective-Context) RAG; adaptive retrieval (SKR); reasoning models with standard RAG (Marco-o1, Skywork-o1); Search-o1 (online search with larger 32B backbone, which it beats by 11.4% CEM on Bamboogle).
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving). Part of the early-2025 lineage of RL-trained agentic search / search-augmented reasoning LLMs (alongside Search-R1, DeepResearcher, and its own follow-up R1-Searcher++), which train LLMs end-to-end with outcome RL to interleave retrieval with reasoning, descending from R1/R1-Zero-style RL-for-reasoning and from iterative RAG-CoT methods.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle over a case base).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
tool_document_engineering: N/A. There is no tool/skill description indexing; retrieval is over Wikipedia document passages, not tool docs. The single search 'tool' is invoked via special query tags with no docstring engineering.
index_content_separation: N/A. No progressive-disclosure index/content separation; passages are retrieved and loaded directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Local index is static (Wikipedia); the search tool is invoked via a custom tag-based protocol (<begin_of_query>/<end_of_query>), not RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling. Online variant calls the Google Web Search API but the index is the live web with no CRUD auto-sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. Single retrieval tool; no inter-tool dependency modeling.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR; no retrieved-case adaptation step). The closest analogue is RL-finetuning of how retrieved documents are used, but no case revision mechanism.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary research paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). For reference: training corpus is KILT 2019 English Wikipedia segmented into 100-word passages (~29M passages); RL training set ~8148 selected samples from HotpotQA + 2WikiMultiHopQA, categorized into easy/medium/difficult by rollout count (Stage-1: 350 medium; Stage-2: ~4561 HotpotQA + ~3581 2Wiki).
